Appearance:
MR SANDEEP R LIMBANI(5977) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 MR MAHESH PUJARA for the Respondent(s) No. 2 MR MANAN MEHTA, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SAMIR J. DAVE  Date : 23/03/2023

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER
Learned Advocate Mr.Mahesh Pujara states that he has instructions to appear for original complainant and he seeks permission to file his appearance on behalf of original complainant.
The permission as prayed for is granted.

1. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties.
2. Rule.
Learned advocates appearing for the respective respondents waive service of Rule on behalf of the respective respondents.

Considering the issue involved in the present application and with consent of the learned advocates appearing for the respective parties as well as considering the fact that the dispute amongst the applicant and complainant has been resolved amicably, this matter is taken up for final disposal forthwith.

sentences.text: By way of this application under section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as "the Code"), the applicant has prayed for quashing and setting aside FIR being C.R.No.11210055201397 of 2020 registered with Salabatpura Police Station, Dist. Surat, for the offence under Sections 406, 420, 120B, 504 and 506(2) of the Indian Penal Code as well as other consequential proceedings arising therefrom.

5. Learned counsel for the respective parties submitted that during pendency of the criminal proceedings, as referred to above, the parties have amicably settled their issue by way of mutual R/CR.MA/1878/2023 ORDER DATED: 23/03/2023 settlement and pursuant to understanding arrived at, the Complainant has accordingly filed an affidavit, which is on record.

The complainant has categorically stated in the affidavit that dispute is amicably resolved and has no objections if the present proceedings are quashed and there is no surviving grievance between them.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties, considering the facts and circumstances arising out of the present application as well as taking into consideration the decisions rendered in th2023e cases of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Anr., reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303, Madan Mohan Abbot Vs. State of Punjab, reported in (2008) 4 SCC 582, Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr., reported in 2009 (1) GLH 31, Manoj Sharma Vs. State &
Ors., reported in 2009 (1) GLH 190 and Narinder Singh & Ors. Vs. State of Punjab & Anr. reported in 2014 (2) Crime 67 (SC), it appears that further continuation of criminal proceedings in R/CR.MA/1878/2023 ORDER DATED: 23/03/2023 relation to the impugned FIR against the applicant would be unnecessary harassment to the applicant.

sentences.text:
It appears that the trial would be futile and further continuance of the proceedings pursuant to the impugned FIR would amount to abuse of process of law and Court and hence, to secure the ends of justice, the impugned FIR and other consequential proceedings are required to be quashed and set aside in exercise of powers conferred under Section 482 of the Code.
7.
Resultantly, this application is allowed.
The impugned FIR being C.R.No.11210055201397 of 2020 registered with Salabatpura Police Station, Dist. Surat, as well as other consequential proceedings
are hereby quashed and set aside qua the present applicant herein.
Accordingly, Rule is made absolute.
Direct service is permitted.

If the applicant is behind bar, Jail authority as well as Court concerned shall take necessary R/CR.MA/1878/2023 ORDER DATED: 23/03/2023 steps to release the accused- applicant from the jail if not required in any other offence.

(SAMIR J. DAVE,J) MEHUL B. TUVAR Rajeshkumar Rupnarayan Sharma vs State Of Gujarat on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84849039/
